The step order contradicts itself. The flow table in feature.md has 8 steps: name, date of birth and first working day together in step 1, then one cross-border step 5 for Germany and Liechtenstein that comes before denomination and children, and a permit-reminder step 8. The 'Questionnaire flow overview' rule and US-01.2 AC-01.2.1 have 10 steps: first working day as its own step 2, Liechtenstein cross-border as step 6, Germany cross-border as step 9 after children, and a 'Summary and submission' step 10. Which order is correct? In particular, are the Germany cross-border questions asked before or after denomination and children, and is there a separate summary step?

Results are 'always derived again from the latest answers'. If HR changes an answer after submission so that new questions now apply, the inputs were never asked. Examples: Single becomes Married (spouse's date of birth, spouse employment), a move from Switzerland to Germany (daily return, certificate), a new child (child block). What should the derived results show while those inputs are missing: no tariff code, an 'incomplete' state, or the old value? Do answers that no longer apply after an HR change get discarded, as they do on employee submission?

Every example in AC-06.6.1, AC-06.6.2 and AC-06.6.3 is marked ❌ under 'Checked', while all other stories show ✅. Are these expected tariff codes (N1Y, C1Y, L0Y, A0N, B0N, 'no tariff code', C1Y with the double taxation agreement note) known to be wrong, or just not checked yet? They are the main acceptance tests for the computed code.

"Answers to questions that no longer apply are discarded on submission (discard_inapplicable_answers), and the questionnaire becomes read-only for the employee (read_only_after_submission)." - Internal snake_case rule ids appear in business prose. D-045 forbids this.

info.message: AC-02.2.1 lists only street, postcode, town and country as required. Its Germany example marks every address field, including country, as only 'asked', while the Switzerland example marks them all 'required'. AC-02.2.2 and D-042 make the house number required too. Are all address fields required for every employee, whatever the country, with 'no house number' as the only way around the house number?

D-036 says answers that no longer apply 'may be kept' until submission. AC-01.5.1 makes it a requirement that the previous answer 'is still there'. Is keeping them a must (testable acceptance criterion), or optional?

In AC-01.2.1, the example 'Employee living in Germany' shows Civil status as '–' in the results, while civil status is always asked of everyone (US-04.1). Is this a mistake in the example, or is civil status meant to be skipped in some case?

Before submission, can the employee save partway and come back later, and is there a review/summary of all answers before the final submit? After submission, does the employee get a confirmation? Submission is final (read-only), so these decide what the employee can check before locking it.

Are there business limits on the first working day, e.g. it must not be in the past or more than N months ahead? Is there a plausibility check on the employee's and spouse's dates of birth (minimum working age)? The pension fund only requires the DD.MM.YYYY format.

Nationality (and the country of the home address and of the spouse's residence) is 'a country by English name'. Which list of countries/nationalities should be offered, and how do stateless employees or employees with unclear status answer the nationality question? Only 'Switzerland vs not' matters for the rule.

The example tables mix 'required' and 'asked' as expected results for questions the text says must be answered. Examples: spouse nationality 'required' for Tomás vs 'asked' for the registered partner; spouse residence 'required' vs 'asked'; in US-05.1, C permit 'required' for Maria vs 'asked' for Tomás. Is there a real difference (i.e. may some of these be left empty), or are they the same?

The spouse's country of residence matters only as 'lives in Switzerland or not'. Under data minimisation (G-01), should we ask the full country, or only 'Does your spouse/partner live in Switzerland? yes/no'?

The permit reminder is 'worded by HR', but no text is given. Who provides the final wording and when (before build or configurable later)? Is it shown only at the end, or also elsewhere (e.g. in a confirmation)?

uncited_units.text: HR meeting transcript Everyone and everything here is fictional. Anna is the HR manager at Muster AG. Leo works in product at Lonio.
Can you hear me okay? You're a bit quiet.
Is this better? I'm in the small meeting room, the big one is taken. Sorry, let me just close the door.
Much better. So, thanks for making the time. The idea today is simple. We want your new employees to give us everything once, so that you stop chasing them for
Yes, please. Right now it's a mess. I have a Word document, then an Excel file, and then I type everything into the portals by hand. Last month I spent a full a
Okay. And how many people do you hire in a year?
Around twenty. More in summer. We're about a hundred and fifty people now, mostly here in Zurich.
Good. Let's start with the biggest pain. What takes you the most time?
Okay, that's clear. And the questionnaire itself is what?
Great. Do you also want a photo? Some customers ask for one.
It could. Do you want that from day one?
We're with Pensionskasse Muster. They have a portal, it's quite old. I'll send you some screenshots of it after this call, that's easier than me explaining it.
Perfect. What do you need for the fund that you don't have?
Sorry, one second, someone's at my door. [pause] Okay, I'm back, sorry. Where were we?
The Julia story. It doesn't matter.
Right. What else about the employee affects the fund? Are they married, things like that?
And what are the options in that list?
Okay. Noted. Can I go back to source tax? You said all non-Swiss employees.
Sure, send it if it's easy. Do people need anything from you on the first day? Laptops, things like that? I just want to see if that belongs in the same form.
Okay. Anything else on who needs to do it? I'd rather hear all of it now.
Only the timing. When can we have this?
I'll come back to you on that this week, once we've gone through your screenshots.
Good. I'll send them after lunch. Thanks, Leo.

questions.question: The step order contradicts itself. The flow table in feature.md has 8 steps: name, date of birth and first working day together in step 1, then one cross-border step 5 for Germany and Liechtenstein that comes before denomination and children, and a permit-reminder step 8. The 'Questionnaire flow overview' rule and US-01.2 AC-01.2.1 have 10 steps: first working day as its own step 2, Liechtenstein cross-border as step 6, Germany cross-border as step 9 after children, and a 'Summary and submission' step 10. Which order is correct? In particular, are the Germany cross-border questions asked before or after denomination and children, and is there a separate summary step?

Results are 'always derived again from the latest answers'. If HR changes an answer after submission so that new questions now apply, the inputs were never asked. Examples: Single becomes Married (spouse's date of birth, spouse employment), a move from Switzerland to Germany (daily return, certificate), a new child (child block). What should the derived results show while those inputs are missing: no tariff code, an 'incomplete' state, or the old value? Do answers that no longer apply after an HR change get discarded, as they do on employee submission?

Every example in AC-06.6.1, AC-06.6.2 and AC-06.6.3 is marked ❌ under 'Checked', while all other stories show ✅. Are these expected tariff codes (N1Y, C1Y, L0Y, A0N, B0N, 'no tariff code', C1Y with the double taxation agreement note) known to be wrong, or just not checked yet? They are the main acceptance tests for the computed code.

AC-02.2.1 lists only street, postcode, town and country as required. Its Germany example marks every address field, including country, as only 'asked', while the Switzerland example marks them all 'required'. AC-02.2.2 and D-042 make the house number required too. Are all address fields required for every employee, whatever the country, with 'no house number' as the only way around the house number?

D-036 says answers that no longer apply 'may be kept' until submission. AC-01.5.1 makes it a requirement that the previous answer 'is still there'. Is keeping them a must (testable acceptance criterion), or optional?

In AC-01.2.1, the example 'Employee living in Germany' shows Civil status as '–' in the results, while civil status is always asked of everyone (US-04.1). Is this a mistake in the example, or is civil status meant to be skipped in some case?

Before submission, can the employee save partway and come back later, and is there a review/summary of all answers before the final submit? After submission, does the employee get a confirmation? Submission is final (read-only), so these decide what the employee can check before locking it.

Are there business limits on the first working day, e.g. it must not be in the past or more than N months ahead? Is there a plausibility check on the employee's and spouse's dates of birth (minimum working age)? The pension fund only requires the DD.MM.YYYY format.

Nationality (and the country of the home address and of the spouse's residence) is 'a country by English name'. Which list of countries/nationalities should be offered, and how do stateless employees or employees with unclear status answer the nationality question? Only 'Switzerland vs not' matters for the rule.

The example tables mix 'required' and 'asked' as expected results for questions the text says must be answered. Examples: spouse nationality 'required' for Tomás vs 'asked' for the registered partner; spouse residence 'required' vs 'asked'; in US-05.1, C permit 'required' for Maria vs 'asked' for Tomás. Is there a real difference (i.e. may some of these be left empty), or are they the same?

The spouse's country of residence matters only as 'lives in Switzerland or not'. Under data minimisation (G-01), should we ask the full country, or only 'Does your spouse/partner live in Switzerland? yes/no'?

The permit reminder is 'worded by HR', but no text is given. Who provides the final wording and when (before build or configurable later)? Is it shown only at the end, or also elsewhere (e.g. in a confirmation)?

review.summary: 12 example simulations fail, all in US-06.6 (the full tariff code). The failures look like one format mismatch: the computed code is split into parts such as ['N', 1, 'Y'], and the expected value is the joined string 'N1Y'. The 'no tariff code' cases return None. This story is the main acceptance test for the computed code, so it must pass before build. The step order is also contradictory between feature.md and US-01.2. Technical terms leak into business prose against D-045. The open questions are non-blocking, but the calculator comparison is a go-live condition.

findings.title: All US-06.6 examples fail (tariff code assembly)
findings.why: The full tariff code is the main output of the feature. Its acceptance examples do not pass, so the rule and the examples disagree. Most likely the rule returns the parts (letter, digit, church suffix) as a list instead of the joined string, and returns None where the spec says 'no tariff code'. The spec side could also be at fault.
findings.evidence: examples: AC-06.6.1 (6 cases), AC-06.6.2 (3 cases), AC-06.6.3 (3 cases). Example: tariff_code = ['N',1,'Y'], expected 'N1Y'. Example: tariff_code = None, expected 'no tariff code'. rule.tariff_letter: the cited fact maps G->Q, but the rule returns null for G.
findings.action: Fix the tariff_code expression so it joins letter, digit and suffix into one string. Decide how 'no tariff code' is represented, either null or an explicit marker, and align the example wording with that. Re-run the examples. Also resolve the G->Q handling in tariff_letter.

findings.title: Step order contradicts itself (8 vs 10 steps)
findings.why: Engineering cannot tell whether the Germany cross-border questions come before or after denomination and children. They also cannot tell whether there is a separate first-working-day step or a summary step.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement on feature.md: the flow table has 8 steps. The questionnaire_flow rule and AC-01.2.1 have 10 steps. trace_judge on rule.questionnaire_flow: the content of steps 1-5 and 7-10 is not backed by cited facts.
findings.action: Add a decision in decisions.yaml fixing the one authoritative step order. Regenerate feature.md and US-01.2 from it.

Keep-answers wording in D-036 versus AC-01.5.1.
